source: 2026-2027 Fantasy Football Analytics (Original) (4).xlsx, sheet 'WRTE Statistics & Graphs'
note: Wide receiver charts from the workbook's WRTE sheet, rows 2-183. The grid's 'High YPRR' and 'High TPRR' columns are 4for4-derived categorisations; §2 rules that vendor's columns out and the operator lifted it for the RB chart and the TE page (docs/STATE.md). Names only here, not the licensed figures. The stickiness and consistency charts come from the operator's nflverse export instead of the workbook, and touch no licensed source at all. Every median, extent, correlation and label order is computed here, not in a component (§11).

targets_airyards.title: Target share against air yards
targets_airyards.caption: Volume and depth are different jobs. Up and to the right is a receiver who is both thrown to often and thrown to deep; far right with a low target share is one running deep routes the quarterback rarely looks at.
notes: Olave: Improved Offense, Elite Yards, Elite Role
Egbuka: Strong Rookie Profile, Evans Departure, Injuries impact in 2025
Smith: WR2 Profile/Performance, Departure of AJB, New OC
McConkey: Departure of Keenan Allen, Healthy O-Line, moving to slot?

airyards_share.title: Air yards share against target share
airyards_share.caption: Both axes are a share of the same offense, so this asks how much of his team's passing game a receiver owns — the downfield share against the total share. Below the diagonal is a possession role, above it a field-stretching one.

groups.label: Dominant Downfield claim with Target Share

wopr_ppg.title: WOPR against PPR points per game
wopr_ppg.caption: Opportunity against what it produced. WOPR weights target share and air yards share into one usage number; the vertical spread at any given WOPR is how much of a receiver's scoring his usage does not explain.
notes: Line of Best Fit: Fair Value PPG Given their role on offense
Below Line of Best Fit: WOPR Usage but no output seen (Room for improvement)
Above Line of Best Fit: Potential Regression/Overplayed role

stickiness.title: What carries into next season
stickiness.caption: Rank correlation between a receiver's season and his next one, across every pair since 2015. The chances a receiver gets come back; what he did with them mostly does not.

consistency.title: Boom weeks against bust weeks
consistency.caption: Each receiver's 2025, as the share of his weeks over 20 PPR points against the share at 5 or under. Bottom left is steady, top right is volatile, and top left is the season everyone wants.

corners.label: Reliable
corners.blurb: Rarely wasted a week, often won one.

corners.label: Floor without a ceiling
corners.blurb: Hard to lose with, hard to win with.

corners.label: Boom or bust
corners.blurb: Real upside, and a real chance of nothing.

corners.label: Neither
corners.blurb: Below the field on both counts.

groups.label: The role says more should be coming
groups.blurb: Top-half usage, bottom-half boom rate. What was missing is the part that repeats least.

groups.label: Outscored the role
groups.blurb: Bottom-half usage, top-half boom rate. The scoring arrived without the workload behind it.

columns.label: Most end-zone looks
columns.blurb: The repeatable half of scoring: who the offense throws to inside the goal line.

columns.label: Scored above their looks
columns.blurb: Touchdowns beyond what their field position accounts for.

columns.label: Scored below their looks
columns.blurb: The looks arrived and the touchdowns did not.

groups.label: Everything points the same way
groups.blurb: A positive column and an offense that backs it. The strongest read on the grid.

groups.label: Flagged in both directions
groups.blurb: Efficient enough to make an efficiency column and expected to score less. Both are true.

groups.label: Scoring flagged to fall, offense behind them
groups.blurb: The touchdown call is the operator's; the scheme is the part likeliest to survive the winter.

groups.label: Positive on the player, nothing from the offense
groups.blurb: The case rests on the receiver alone — no scheme column argues for him.

groups.label: Flagged to fall, with nothing offsetting
groups.blurb: A regression call and no column anywhere else on the grid pointing the other way.
